title: PDIM, PGL, and the virulence envelope
dek: Phthiocerol dimycocerosates and phenolic glycolipids are not mycolates. Labs lose PDIM in H37Rv stocks; genomes lose pps/mas/fadD26 and look attenuated for the wrong reason.
story: PDIM (phthiocerol dimycocerosate) and related phenolic glycolipids sit in the outer leaflet of the mycobacterial envelope. They are not mycolic acids. They modulate macrophage signalling, mask PAMPs, and are required for full virulence in most animal models. The biosynthetic locus (ppsA–E, mas, fadD26, mmpL7 and neighbours) is a mutational sink in laboratory passage.

H37Rv stocks silently lose PDIM. A macrophage-killing or mouse-survival paper that does not TLC or sequence the PDIM locus is comparing two envelopes, not two genotypes of interest. Clinical isolates keep PDIM because transmission selects for it.

PGL variants (PGL-tb in some L2 strains) are lineage-structured. Do not call a Beijing isolate “hypervirulent” from PGL presence alone; do not call an L4 isolate “attenuated” because it lacks that PGL. Envelope lipids are covariates, not a DST.
deepTitle: What to sequence when the mouse looks weird
deep: pps and mas frameshifts are the usual lab-stock signature. They will also appear in a WGS BAM if you look.
mmpL7 exporters PDIM; it is not mmpL5 (the BDQ/CFZ efflux partner of rv0678).
PDIM-negative mutants can look more inflammatory in vitro and less persistent in vivo. Phenotype direction depends on the assay.
Do not bulk-copy Mycobrowser gene comments into a report. Name the locus and the frameshift.

visual.caption: PDIM/PGL sit outside the mycolate–arabinogalactan core. Losing them is a stock artefact more often than a treatment target.

example.title: Attenuated H37Rv that is still katG WT
example.setup: A knockout looks hyper-killed in macrophages versus “H37Rv.” TLC shows no PDIM in the parent.

steps.title: Blame the parent first
steps.body: Re-sequence pps/mas or replace the stock before writing a virulence paper.

steps.title: Not an INH story
steps.body: katG WT is irrelevant to PDIM loss.

steps.title: Clinical isolates
steps.body: Fresh MTBC from sputum almost always keeps PDIM. The artefact is the freezer.

example.takeaway: PDIM is virulence chemistry and a stock-hygiene check, not a first-line drug target.

choices: A mycolic acid species inhibited by INH
A phthiocerol dimycocerosate distinct from mycolates
check.answer: A phthiocerol dimycocerosate distinct from mycolates
check.why: Mycolates are FAS-II products. PDIM is a different biosynthetic island.

check.prompt: A lab H37Rv passaged 80 times on plates is most likely to have lost:
choices: the entire ESX-1 RD1 as in BCG
check.why: PDIM loss is the classic H37Rv freezer artefact. RD1 loss is BCG’s construction, not random passage.

check.prompt: On the layered envelope, PDIM is drawn:
choices: In the cytosol next to ATP synthase
As an outermost lipid leaflet above mycolates
check.answer: As an outermost lipid leaflet above mycolates
check.why: That placement is the teaching point: outside the INH/EMB core.
